title: Repository, project skeletons and CI
summary: git init, three projects, generated bindings, a build that runs itself
description:
CURRENT STATE: /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter is EMPTY and NOT a git repository. `git init` happens in this phase. Depends on F007 (tools installed) and follows F001 (platform facts established).

Replaces the phase originally placed in F006 (store distribution), which was the wrong home — setting up a project and shipping it to stores are different jobs.

REPOSITORY LAYOUT — the decision this phase must make. One repo holding the Rust core plus both apps, or separate repos. Not cosmetic: it determines how UniFFI bindings and packaged datasets flow from the core to the two apps. One repo keeps them in step and makes CI simple; separate repos need a publishing step and let the apps sit on a stale core silently.

PROJECT SKELETONS:
- Rust core crate, buildable and testable on the HOST from day one. F002 is pure logic with no platform dependency, so its tests must run with no device or simulator — that is the fast feedback loop and it should stay fast.
- Xcode project with THREE targets: host app, Call Directory extension (P008), SMS filter extension (P009). Both extensions link the same core and run under tight memory limits.
- Android Gradle project linking the same core through JNI via cargo-ndk.

PROVE IT END TO END: a trivial core function called successfully from Swift AND from Kotlin. That one call validates the toolchain, all seven targets, the linking and the binding generation together — and it should pass before any real core work starts in F002.

CI: build the core per target, run core tests on the host, generate bindings, build both apps, run F003's dataset converter and FAIL THE BUILD on validation errors. A silently truncated dataset makes rules stop matching with no error anywhere, which is close to undebuggable in the field. Explicitly NOT automated: F001/T001's measurement harness needs real hardware and human observation.

CONVENTIONS: formatting, linting, test layout, dependency policy — including how upstream libphonenumber data updates are pulled in, since that data is an input to F003's converter and not a checked-in artifact.

BEHAVIOURS TO PRESERVE: generated bindings and packaged datasets are build outputs, never committed. Track the core's binary size per target, since an oversized core makes the iOS extensions unviable regardless of correctness.
notes:
**Handoff context update:**
T007 (repository) and T008 (both app skeletons linking the core) are done and committed on main as c1b0a3b and 5f62074. The Rust core builds for all seven targets, UniFFI generates Swift and Kotlin bindings during the build, and the iOS app running on the user's iPhone displays values read across the FFI from Rust — Swift genuinely calls the core. The Android APK builds and carries the core for all three ABIs.

**Remaining work:**
T009 — CI and shared conventions. Build the core per target, run its tests on the host, generate bindings, build both apps, fail the build on dataset validation errors once F003 exists, agree formatting/linting/test layout/dependency policy, and track core binary size per target. Consider a lint enforcing Guidelines §1. Do not automate F001/T001's measurement harness. Also open: the Kotlin call has only been proven at compile time — no Android device or emulator is available to run it.
decisions: One repository holding the core and both apps, because the apps are thin shells and a core change plus its regenerated bindings should land in one commit
Nothing generated is committed — bindings, XCFramework, cargo-ndk output and the xcodegen-produced .xcodeproj are all gitignored
AGP 9 on Gradle 9 with the separate kotlin.android plugin omitted, because the installed JDK 26 cannot be used by AGP 8.x or Gradle 8.x and the user declined installing an older JDK
ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO set project-wide, because Xcode 26 Debug builds leave the extension principal class out of the .appex and the extension then fails to enable
Kotlin bindings generated from the host library rather than the Android .so, because the release profile strips and stripping removes UniFFI metadata from ELF objects while Mach-O retains it
The exported function is core_version rather than version, because a bare version collides with NSObject.version inside any class inheriting from it, which both iOS extensions do

tasks.title: Create the repository and decide its layout
tasks.description:
First code-bearing action in the project. Depends on F007 (tools installed) and follows F001 (verification done).

CURRENT STATE: /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter is EMPTY and is NOT a git repository. `git init` happens here.

THE DECISION THIS TASK EXISTS TO MAKE — repository layout. One repo holding the Rust core plus both apps, or separate repos. It is not cosmetic: it determines how UniFFI bindings and packaged datasets flow from the core to the two apps.
- One repo: core and apps always in step, CI is simple, a core change and its binding regeneration land in one commit. Downside: iOS and Android developers carry the whole tree.
- Separate repos: needs a publishing step for the core artifact, and the apps can silently sit on a stale core.
RECOMMENDATION: one repo. The core is small, the apps are thin shells over it, and Guidelines §3 puts all logic in the core — so the core changes far more often than the shells, and keeping them in lockstep is the common case rather than the exception.

WORK:
- git init, .gitignore covering Rust target/, Xcode build products and user state, Gradle build output, and — importantly — GENERATED UNIFFI BINDINGS and PACKAGED DATASETS. Both are build outputs. Checked-in bindings drift from the core silently and only fail at runtime on one platform; a checked-in dataset defeats R5's versioning.
- Directory layout reflecting the decision above.
- Cargo workspace for the core crate, building and testing on the host.
- README recording the layout decision and its reasoning, so the next person does not relitigate it.

DO NOT: create the Xcode or Android project skeletons here, and do not set up CI. Those are separate tasks in this phase. This task ends with a repository holding a Rust core that builds and tests on the host.

EDGE CASE: the directory already exists and is empty — git init in place, do not create a nested directory.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-08. Repository exists, core builds and tests on the host, first commit made.

DECISION — ONE REPOSITORY holding the core and both apps. Recorded in README.md with the reasoning, so it is not relitigated. Rationale: the apps are thin shells and all filtering logic is in the core by Guidelines §3, so the core changes far more often than the shells and a core change plus its regenerated bindings should land in one commit. Separate repos would need a publishing step and would let an app sit silently on a stale core. The cost — both platform developers carry the whole tree — is small by comparison.

LAYOUT CREATED at /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter:
  core/src/lib.rs     the engine (skeleton)
  core/Cargo.toml     callerfilter-core
  Cargo.toml          workspace
  tools/  docs/       empty, for the dataset converter and design notes
  README.md
  .gitignore
The iOS and Android projects join in T008.

COMMIT c1b0a3b — 39 files. Includes .planner/ deliberately: the plan is the project's source of truth and the README points at it.

CARGO SETUP:
- Workspace with resolver 2, edition 2021, rust-version 1.90.
- core crate-type = ["lib", "staticlib", "cdylib"] — rlib for host tests, staticlib/cdylib for iOS linking and the Android JNI.
- phonenumber 0.3 declared as a workspace dependency (parse/validate/format; it has no geocoder, which we write ourselves in F002).
- Release profile tuned for SIZE not speed: opt-level="z", lto, codegen-units=1, strip, panic=abort. Reason: the iOS Call Directory and SMS filter extensions run under tight memory limits, so the core's binary size matters more than it would in an ordinary app. Revisit if profiling shows the Android 5-second screening budget is at risk.

CODE WRITTEN — deliberately minimal, this task is scaffolding not F002:
- Decision enum (Allow / Block / Silence / Label) with the platform asymmetries documented on it — Silence is Android-only, Label is iOS-calls-only.
- EntryLimit newtype carrying the measured iOS cap. Default is 1,800,000, chosen near the measured ~2,000,000 cap rather than conservatively, because the only cost of a bigger list is a one-off background load paid at enable/reload time, never at call time. The doc comment states plainly that this is a starting estimate, that only one device was measured, that the shell must back off on error 5, and that it must never be shown to the user.
- version() placeholder so the crate and its test harness exist from day one.
- Two tests, both passing on the host with no device or simulator. One asserts the default limit stays under the measured cap — a guard against someone raising it carelessly later.

GITIGNORE — two entries matter more than the rest and carry comments saying why: generated UniFFI bindings (drift from the core in silence, fail at runtime on one platform only) and packaged datasets (a committed one defeats R5's over-the-air versioning, and a silently truncated one makes rules stop matching with no error anywhere). Signing material and keystores are also excluded.

VERIFIED: `cargo test` passes, 2 tests, no device or simulator involved. `git check-ignore` confirms target/ is excluded.

NOT DONE HERE, by design: Xcode and Android project skeletons (T008), CI and conventions (T009).

NOTE FOR T008: F001's four build traps apply directly — Xcode 26 Debug builds put extension code in a separate __preview.dylib so the extension fails to enable (build Release or set ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO); xcodegen's info.path silently drops a hand-written NSExtension dictionary (use info.properties); handle context.isIncremental or hit sqlite constraint errors; retry on CallKit error 7.

tasks.title: Xcode and Android project skeletons linking the core
tasks.description:
Stand up both app projects so they compile against the Rust core through UniFFI. Depends on the repository task, and on F001/T002 having established what shape the Android app actually needs to be.

CURRENT STATE: nothing exists. Xcode with iOS SDK 26.2 is present; the Android SDK arrives with F007.

XCODE PROJECT — THREE TARGETS, not one:
- Host app (SwiftUI).
- Call Directory extension (CXCallDirectoryProvider) — see P008(F004).
- SMS filter extension (ILMessageFilterExtension) — see P009(F004).
Both extensions link the same core. They run under tight memory limits, so treat the core's binary size and load cost as a build output watched from the first day rather than something discovered when an extension gets killed in the field.

SIGNING, CURRENT CONSTRAINT: no paid Apple Developer account. Free personal-team provisioning, 7-day certificates, own devices only, NO App Groups. Set the skeleton up so it builds under those limits. The real app WILL need an App Group to share rules between host and extensions (R2, R4), so a paid account is a hard prerequisite before F004 is functional. If F007 found that free teams cannot run extensions at all, stop and report.

ANDROID PROJECT: Gradle project linking the same core through JNI, with cargo-ndk producing the per-ABI libraries. CHECK F001/T002'S FINDING FIRST — if blocking an SMS requires becoming the default SMS app, the Android app is a materially different shape and that is a product decision, not something to work around while scaffolding.

UNIFFI BINDINGS ARE GENERATED BY THE BUILD, NEVER COMMITTED. The single most important convention here. Checked-in bindings drift from the core in silence and surface as a runtime failure on one platform only. Wire generation into both builds now, while the projects are empty and it is easy.

PROVE IT WORKS END TO END: a trivial core function called successfully from Swift and from Kotlin. That one call validates the toolchain, all seven targets, the linking and the binding generation together. Do this before any real core work in F002.

DO NOT: implement filtering logic here — that is F002, and Guidelines §3 keeps it in the core regardless.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-09-08. Both apps build against the shared Rust core through UniFFI. Commit 5f62074.

VERIFIED END TO END ON iOS: the app running on the user's iPhone displays "core 0.1.0" and "iOS entry limit 1800000", both read across the FFI from the Rust core. Swift is genuinely calling Rust, not a stub.

PARTIALLY VERIFIED ON ANDROID: the app compiles against the generated Kotlin bindings — which fails if the API surface does not match — and the APK carries libcallerfilter_core.so for all three ABIs plus JNA's libjnidispatch.so. NOT executed: no Android device or emulator is available, so the Kotlin call is proven at compile and packaging time only. Tracked as an open checklist item; run it when Android hardware or an emulator image exists.

WHAT EXISTS NOW:
- apps/ios/project.yml — xcodegen source of truth for three targets: CallerFilter (app), CallDirectoryExtension, MessageFilterExtension. The .xcodeproj is generated and gitignored; edit the yml, not the project.
- apps/android/ — Gradle project, AGP 9 on Gradle 9.
- tools/build-ios.sh — builds three iOS targets, lipos the simulator slices, generates Swift bindings, packages an XCFramework, prints core size per slice.
- tools/build-android.sh — cargo-ndk for three ABIs, generates Kotlin bindings, installs/locates the NDK, prints size per ABI.

BUNDLE IDENTIFIERS ARE LOAD-BEARING, chosen deliberately:
  com.antoniopantano.callerfilter
  com.antoniopantano.callerfilter.calldirectory
  com.antoniopantano.callerfilter.messagefilter
The app passes the Call Directory one to CXCallDirectoryManager.reloadExtension(withIdentifier:), so renaming it later means changing code.

MEASURED SIZES:
- iOS linked binaries: app 528K, each extension 492K, whole .app 1.6M.
- Android core: 232K armeabi-v7a, 332K arm64-v8a, 364K x86_64. Debug APK 5.4M.
- The 49M static .a is PRE-LINK NOISE, not a real cost — verified by rebuilding without the phonenumber dependency and getting the same 49M. Judge size from linked binaries only.

FIVE PROBLEMS SOLVED, each now fixed in the build files with a comment explaining why:
1. ENABLE_DEBUG_DYLIB=NO is set project-wide. Xcode 26 Debug builds put target code in a separate __preview.dylib, leaving the extension's principal class out of the .appex so it fails to enable with a generic error. Carried forward from T001.
2. `version` was renamed to `core_version` in Rust. The Swift bindings land in the same module as app code, and a bare `version` collides with NSObject.version inside any class inheriting from it — which both extensions do. Renaming in the core stops it recurring anywhere.
3. Kotlin bindings are generated from the HOST library, not the Android .so. The release profile strips, and stripping removes the metadata UniFFI reads from an ELF object. Mach-O retains it, which is why the iOS build can read its own artifact. Bindings describe the crate's interface, not the target, so the host library is a correct source.
4. TOOLCHAIN VERSION BIND: the installed JDK is 26 (Homebrew openjdk). AGP 8.x cannot parse it and Gradle 8.x does not support it, so the project uses AGP 9 on Gradle 9. AGP 9 bundles Kotlin, so the separate org.jetbrains.kotlin.android plugin must be omitted or it fails with "extension already registered with name 'kotlin'". The user declined installing an older JDK; this combination works without one.
5. Generated Kotlin sources must go on the KOTLIN source set (sourceSets["main"].kotlin.srcDir), not the java one. Under AGP 9 java.srcDir does not reach the Kotlin compiler and the bindings appear as unresolved references.

CONVENTION ENFORCED: generated bindings, the XCFramework, cargo-ndk output and the generated .xcodeproj are all gitignored. Nothing generated is committed.

NOT DONE HERE, by design: CI and shared conventions (T009). No filtering logic — that is F002, and Guidelines §3 keeps it in the core regardless. The extensions contain only a call to core_version() to prove linkage.

SIGNING NOTE: builds under the free personal team (UY66NT5LGF) with no App Group, as required. F004 will need an App Group to share rules between the app and its extensions, and that needs a paid account — still a hard prerequisite before the real iOS app can work.

tasks.title: CI and shared conventions
tasks.description:
Make the build run itself, and settle the conventions once so they are not argued per pull request. Depends on the project skeletons task.

CI SHAPE:
- Build the Rust core for every target: three iOS, three Android, plus host.
- Run the core's tests on the HOST. F002 is pure logic with no platform dependency, so its tests need no device or simulator — this is the fast feedback loop and it should stay fast.
- Generate UniFFI bindings (never committed — see the skeletons task).
- Build both apps.
- Run F003's dataset converter and FAIL THE BUILD on its validation errors. A silently truncated dataset makes rules stop matching with no error anywhere in the system, which is close to undebuggable in the field.

EXPLICITLY NOT AUTOMATED: F001/T001's measurement harness needs a real iPhone and human observation of memory and kill behaviour. Do not try to run it in CI.

SHARED CONVENTIONS, agreed here and written down:
- Formatting and linting for Rust, Swift and Kotlin.
- Test layout and naming. Note where the weight belongs: P002(F002) says the rule model carries the heaviest coverage in the project, because a bug there is a bug on every platform simultaneously.
- Dependency policy, including how libphonenumber upstream data updates are pulled in — that data is an input to F003's converter, not a checked-in artifact.

A CONVENTION WORTH ENFORCING MECHANICALLY: Project Guidelines §1 forbids country codes, number lengths, prefixes and place names in source files. That is checkable — a lint or test that greps for suspicious literals in the core would catch the most likely violation of the project's central rule. Consider adding it rather than trusting review.

ALSO: track the core's binary size per target as a CI output. The iOS extensions run under tight memory limits and an oversized core makes them unviable regardless of correctness.

handoff:
# Repository and both app skeletons done; CI (T009) is next

Created at: 2026-09-08
Updated at: 2026-09-08
Reason: T007 and T008 are complete and committed. Handing off before T009 so the traps already paid for are not rediscovered — every one of them recurs in CI.

## Current focus

**P018(F008)/T009 — CI and shared conventions.** The only task left in this phase. T007 and T008 are done, nothing is half-finished, the tree is clean.

## What was being done

- **T007** — repository created on `main`. One-repo layout, Cargo workspace, `callerfilter-core` crate, `.gitignore` excluding every generated artifact, README recording the layout decision. Commit `c1b0a3b`.
- **T008** — both app skeletons linking the core through UniFFI. Commit `5f62074`.
  - iOS: three targets (app, Call Directory extension, message filter extension). Built Release, installed on the user's iPhone, **verified at runtime** — it displays `core 0.1.0` and `iOS entry limit 1800000`, both read across the FFI from Rust.
  - Android: AGP 9 Gradle project. APK builds and carries `libcallerfilter_core.so` for all three ABIs. **Never executed** — no Android device or emulator.
  - `tools/build-ios.sh` and `tools/build-android.sh` perform the whole per-platform pipeline including binding generation and size reporting.

## How to resume

First action: `cd /Users/antonio/projects/caller-filter && cargo test` — expect 2 passing tests, no device. Confirms the tree is intact.

Then read Blockers before writing any CI, and export these — they are in no shell profile:

```sh
export ANDROID_HOME=/opt/homebrew/share/android-commandlinetools
export ANDROID_NDK_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/29.0.14206865
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk     # JDK 26
```

Commands that work today:

```sh
cargo test                                  # host, 2 tests, no device
./tools/build-ios.sh                        # 3 targets, lipo, bindings, XCFramework
./tools/build-android.sh                    # cargo-ndk 3 ABIs, Kotlin bindings
cd apps/ios && xcodegen generate && \
  xcodebuild -scheme CallerFilter -configuration Release -allowProvisioningUpdates build
cd apps/android && gradle :app:assembleDebug   # system gradle 9.7.1, NOT a wrapper
```

Installed: Rust 1.96 + 6 mobile targets, Android SDK (platform 36, sources 36, build-tools 36.0.0, NDK 29), cargo-ndk 4.1.2, xcodegen 2.46, gradle 9.7.1, Xcode 26.3.

## Files touched

```
core/src/lib.rs                     core_version, default_entry_limit, EntryLimit, Decision
core/src/bin/uniffi-bindgen.rs      binding generator
Cargo.toml, core/Cargo.toml
apps/ios/project.yml                xcodegen source of truth — edit this, never the .xcodeproj
apps/ios/CallerFilter/App.swift
apps/ios/CallDirectoryExtension/CallDirectoryHandler.swift
apps/ios/MessageFilterExtension/MessageFilterExtension.swift
```

3. **Toolchain version bind.** Installed JDK is 26. AGP 8.x cannot parse that version and Gradle 8.x does not support it, so the project uses AGP 9 + Gradle 9. 4. **Generated Kotlin goes on the `kotlin` source set**, not `java`. Under AGP 9, `java.srcDir` does not reach the Kotlin compiler and bindings appear as unresolved references.

## Recent decisions

- **One repository** holding core and both apps. The apps are thin shells, all logic is in the core, so the core changes far more often and a core change plus regenerated bindings should land in one commit. Rejected: separate repos, which need a publishing step and let an app sit silently on a stale core.
- **Nothing generated is committed.** Bindings drift from the core in silence and fail at runtime on one platform only; a committed dataset defeats over-the-air versioning.
- **Release profile tuned for size** (`opt-level="z"`, LTO, strip, panic=abort) because the iOS extensions run under tight memory limits. Note strip is exactly what breaks ELF binding generation — blocker 2.
- **`core_version`, not `version`.** A bare `version` collides with `NSObject.version` inside any class inheriting from it, which both iOS extensions do. Renamed in Rust so it cannot recur anywhere.
- **Extension bundle identifiers are load-bearing.** The app passes `com.antoniopantano.callerfilter.calldirectory` to `reloadExtension(withIdentifier:)`, so renaming means changing code.
